Package game.plants

Class Plant

java.lang.Object
edu.monash.fit2099.engine.GameEntity
edu.monash.fit2099.engine.positions.Ground
game.plants.Plant
All Implemented Interfaces:
Printable, Regressible
Direct Known Subclasses:
CauliflowerSprout, Crop, MelonSprout, StrawberrySeedling, StrawberrySprout
public abstract class Plant extends Ground implements Regressible
Abstract base class for every plant, at any growth stage.

A plant is a type of Ground with its own age: it is 0 when the plant is placed on the map and goes up by 1 every turn. Only the plant itself changes its age, so there is no setter.

Each plant has a list of abilities in priority order. Every turn it tries them from the highest priority down and stops at the first one that actually does something, so a plant does at most one thing per turn (attemptGrowth(edu.monash.fit2099.engine.positions.Location)). What it did is displayed to the player; a turn where nothing happens is not reported. While the plant has a GrowthPausedStatus, it still ages but does not try any of its abilities.

Every plant is Regressible. By default a regressed plant dies and its tile becomes Dirt, as when a crop is removed; plants with an earlier growth stage override previousStage() to return it instead.

    • attemptGrowth

      public String attemptGrowth(Location location)
      Tries this plant's abilities, from the highest priority down, and stops at the first one that does something. While the plant's growth is paused, no ability is tried, so every caller (the plant's own turn or a magical effect) obeys the pause. Does not age the plant and does not display the result, so a caller forcing an extra growth attempt (e.g. a magical effect) gets the description back to use however it needs to, instead of this plant ageing an extra turn or the result being printed twice.
      Parameters:
      location - the location of this plant
      Returns:
      a description of what happened, or "" if no ability did anything

    • forceGrowth

      public String forceGrowth(Location location)
      Tries this plant's abilities immediately, the same way attemptGrowth(edu.monash.fit2099.engine.positions.Location) does, except each ability skips its own gating (such as an interval or a chance roll) via PlantAbility.forcePerform(game.plants.Plant, edu.monash.fit2099.engine.positions.Location). Still obeys a GrowthPausedStatus, and still does not age the plant or display the result, for the same reasons attemptGrowth(edu.monash.fit2099.engine.positions.Location) does not: the caller forcing this (e.g. a magical effect) decides how to use the description itself.
      Parameters:
      location - the location of this plant
      Returns:
      a description of what happened, or "" if no ability did anything
